sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Eochaid mac Eirc was the husband of the goddess Tailtiu. He stands as the ideal king of early Irish legend. In his reign the land bore fruit in plenty. Rain fell so gently that it seemed like dew. No man ever told a lie in his days. He ruled the midland kingship among the Fir Bolg. Either he or Eochaid Garbh set the Lughnasa fair at Teltown in honor of Tailtiu. The memory of his honest rule outlasted his reign.
